sector_classification.cyclicality: highly cyclical commodity producer, somewhat countercyclical to broader equities/USD

overview: AngloGold Ashanti is one of the world's largest gold producers, operating ten continuing mining operations across Africa (Ghana, DRC, Egypt, Guinea, Tanzania), Australia, and the Americas (Argentina, Brazil), supported by greenfield exploration projects in Colombia and Nevada. Originally a South African company (AngloGold Ashanti Limited), it redomiciled to the UK as AngloGold Ashanti plc in 2023, moved its primary listing to the NYSE with secondary listings in Johannesburg and Ghana, and relocated its group headquarters to Denver, Colorado. The company produced 3.09 million ounces of gold in FY2025 and generated record free cash flow of ~$2.9 billion as gold prices surged to record levels.

business_model.summary: AngloGold Ashanti mines, processes, and sells gold doré/bullion into the spot gold market, with silver and other minor metals as by-product credits. Revenue is purely commodity/transactional, driven by ounces produced and the prevailing spot gold price rather than recurring or contracted revenue; the company does not typically hedge gold price exposure at the corporate level, giving shareholders full leverage to gold price moves. The November 2024 acquisition of Centamin (Sukari mine, Egypt) added a Tier 1 asset contributing ~16% of group production and materially changed the portfolio's scale and geographic/NCI structure.

revenue_streams.name: Gold
revenue_streams.trend: growing - record FY2025 revenue of $9.9bn (+71% YoY) driven primarily by record gold prices plus Sukari/Obuasi volume contribution

revenue_streams.name: Silver and other by-products
revenue_streams.trend: stable - $163m of by-product revenue in FY2025 against $9,893m total product revenue

business_model.customer_type: B2B - gold sold as doré/bullion into global spot and refined-metal markets (banks, refiners, bullion dealers); no significant customer concentration risk given gold's fungibility
business_model.geographic_mix: Ten continuing operations: Ghana (Obuasi, Iduapriem), Tanzania (Geita), DRC (Kibali joint venture), Egypt (Sukari), Guinea, Australia (Sunrise Dam, Tropicana), and the Americas (Argentina - Cerro Vanguardia; Brazil - Serra Grande), plus greenfield exploration in Colombia (Gramalote) and Nevada, USA

competitive_position.market_position: One of the world's top gold producers by volume (~3.0-3.17 million ounces guided for FY2026), but sits at the higher end of the major-producer cost curve; Sukari (Egypt) is now a Tier 1 asset generating ~$1.3bn adjusted EBITDA in FY2025, while Obuasi (Ghana) is mid-ramp toward a 400,000 oz/year target by 2028

moat_factors.description: Ten operating mines across four continents reduce single-asset/single-country concentration risk relative to peers with fewer, larger assets, though this comes at the cost of less economy of scale per site

moat_factors.factor: Tier 1 long-life assets (Sukari, Geita, Obuasi, Kibali)
moat_factors.description: Large reserve bases and multi-decade mine lives at flagship assets provide long-term production visibility and underpin reserve replacement
As one of the largest listed gold producers, AU offers significant unhedged leverage to gold prices, attracting investors seeking pure-play gold exposure
Decades of operating experience and government relationships in Ghana, Tanzania, Guinea and DRC provide some advantage in navigating permitting and community relations versus newer entrants

weaknesses: Highest-cost producer among major gold peers: Q2 2026 AISC of $2,039/oz versus Newmont's ~$1,621/oz and Barrick's ~$1,866/oz, compressing margins relative to peers at the same gold price
Heavy concentration in politically higher-risk African jurisdictions (Ghana, DRC, Tanzania, Guinea, Egypt) exposed to resource nationalism, royalty hikes, and local-ownership mandates
Obuasi remains mid-ramp-up and suffered a fatal underground incident in April 2026 that closed the KMS shaft, illustrating ongoing operational/geotechnical execution risk
No corporate-level gold price hedging means full downside exposure if gold prices correct sharply
Complex multi-jurisdiction cost base (JV interests at Kibali, NCI from Centamin deal) complicates cost control and capital allocation discipline

growth_drivers: Obuasi (Ghana) ramp-up toward 400,000 oz/year by 2028 via a >$1 billion modernization, expansion and recapitalization program, with higher-grade Block 11 access targeted around 2029

Sukari (Egypt) integration following the Centamin acquisition, now a Tier 1 asset producing a record ~500,000 oz in FY2025 (~16% of group production) with ongoing discussions with Egyptian regulators (MRMIA) to expand production and extend mine life

Record gold price environment ($4,000-4,500+/oz in 2026, with Goldman Sachs/JPMorgan forecasting $4,900-5,400/oz into 2027) providing substantial operating leverage and record free cash flow ($2.9bn FY2025, +204% YoY)
Greenfield exploration pipeline in Colombia (Gramalote) and Nevada, USA, diversifying the portfolio toward lower-risk jurisdictions
New $2 billion share buyback program (approved July 2026) aligning capital returns with North American peers, alongside a growing base dividend ($1.8bn declared FY2025)
Balance sheet deleveraging - $666 million bond repurchase completed April 2026, reducing gross debt and eliminating 2028/2030 maturities
Continued exploration success and reserve replacement across Geita (Tanzania), Kibali (DRC) and Iduapriem (Ghana) extending mine lives

business.description: April 2026 fatality at Obuasi from an underground ore-pass waste release closed the KMS shaft; prior 2025 Obuasi security incident (army/illegal miner clash, 7 killed) also disrupted operations, highlighting recurring safety and operational risk in underground and remote African operations
AISC of ~$1,780-1,990/oz guided for FY2026 versus Newmont (~$1,621-1,680/oz) and Barrick (~$1,866/oz) means AU's margins compress faster than peers' in a gold price pullback

Simultaneously ramping Obuasi, integrating Sukari, and managing a JV interest at Kibali (DRC) and legacy assets spread across ten mines in four continents strains management bandwidth and capital allocation discipline
Security incidents involving illegal miners (galamsey) at Ghanaian operations pose ongoing safety, legal and reputational risk

financial.description: Revenue and cash flow are fully exposed to spot gold price moves in both directions, amplifying earnings volatility

financial.risk: Currency and local cost inflation exposure
financial.description: Costs are partly denominated in South African rand, Ghanaian cedi, Tanzanian shilling, Australian dollar, Argentine peso and other local currencies, creating FX translation risk and local inflation pass-through even though revenue is USD-denominated gold
Sustaining capital expenditure rose to $332m in Q2 2026 from $273m in Q2 2025, a key driver of AISC increases even as production volumes softened

regulatory.description: Ghana introduced a sliding-scale gold royalty of 5-12% (reaching the 12% ceiling at $4,500/oz gold, near current spot levels) and requires foreign operators to transition operational control of mining services to Ghanaian-owned contractors by December 2026, directly affecting AU's two Ghanaian mines (Obuasi, Iduapriem)

DRC has tightened state oversight/royalty enforcement via Gécamines, and Tanzania has expanded local-content and export requirements; both trends raise the cost and complexity of operating the Kibali JV and other regional interests

Ongoing negotiations with Egypt's Mineral Resources and Mining Industries Authority (MRMIA) over production expansion and mine-life extension create approval and fiscal-term uncertainty for the newly Tier-1 Sukari asset

Record gold prices are prompting multiple African governments to revisit royalty and state-participation terms negotiated in leaner times, a pattern likely to continue as long as gold remains elevated

macro.description: Current record gold prices ($4,000-4,500+/oz) reflect central bank buying, rate-cut expectations, and geopolitical/fiscal concerns; a reversal in any of these drivers (e.g., faster-than-expected Fed tightening, resolution of geopolitical tensions, slower central bank purchases) would directly compress AU's margins given its above-average cost base
As with all gold producers, a strengthening dollar is typically a headwind to gold prices, though AU's local-currency cost base (rand, cedi, shilling) provides a partial natural offset
Gold is non-yielding, so the opportunity cost of holding it falls as real rates decline; a shift toward higher real rates would reduce investment demand for gold and pressure prices

execution.description: Obuasi produced 266,000 oz in 2026 against a 400,000 oz/year target by 2028; infrastructure completion (vertical shafts) and the KMS shaft closure following the April 2026 fatality add execution risk to the modernization program

Though integration has gone well to date (Sukari delivered record production and ~$475m FCF in FY2025), extracting full synergies and managing the enlarged NCI/JV structure over time remains a multi-year execution task

Balancing the new $2 billion buyback program, a growing dividend, Obuasi capex, and debt reduction requires sustained capital discipline, particularly if gold prices were to retreat from current highs

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold prices are at record highs (~$4,000-4,500+/oz in 2026) driven by sustained central bank buying (forecast ~755 tonnes in 2026, well above the pre-2022 average of 400-500 tonnes), Fed rate-cut expectations, and geopolitical/fiscal uncertainty eroding confidence in the US dollar; major banks (Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, UBS, Standard Chartered) forecast further gains to $4,900-5,400+/oz through 2027, which would continue to benefit unhedged producers like AU
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - gold mining is a cyclical commodity business, but gold itself is often counter-cyclical/defensive relative to broader risk assets, acting as a hedge against inflation, currency debasement and geopolitical stress; AU's earnings are highly leveraged to the gold price given its above-average cost structure
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High (inverse) - gold is a non-yielding asset, so falling real interest rates and a dovish Fed increase its relative attractiveness and have been a major driver of the current price cycle; rising real rates would be a meaningful headwind
key_input_costs: Labor (South Africa, Ghana, Tanzania, DRC, Australia)
Sustaining and growth capital for Obuasi shaft infrastructure

recent_developments.event: Completed $2.5 billion acquisition of Centamin, adding the Sukari mine in Egypt and ~500,000 oz/year of potential production
Security incident at Obuasi involving Ghanaian army and illegal miners (galamsey) resulted in 7 deaths, raising community/security risk profile

Record FY2025 results: revenue of $9.9bn (+71% YoY), free cash flow of $2.9bn (+204% YoY), and record dividend declared of $1.8bn, driven by record gold prices and Sukari's first full year of production (record 500,000 oz, $1.3bn adjusted EBITDA)
Fatal incident at Obuasi (contractor killed by release of waste material from an underground ore pass) led to closure of the KMS shaft; comprehensive multidisciplinary investigation launched
Completed repurchase of ~$666 million of outstanding bonds, reducing gross debt and eliminating portions of 2028 and 2030 maturities

Q1 2026 results and dividend declaration; company reiterated it expects to meet FY2026 production guidance near the midpoint (~3.0 Moz) despite the Obuasi KMS shaft closure, aided by strong performance at other assets
Shareholders approved a new $2 billion share buyback program, aligning capital returns with North American gold-mining peers

Q2 2026 results: EBITDA +46% YoY to $2.0bn, free cash flow +36% YoY to $727m, basic EPS of $1.97 (+49% YoY), headline earnings +58% YoY to $1.01bn; interim dividend of 72c/share declared ($364m), bringing H1 2026 dividends to $949m (188c/share) versus $469m (92.5c/share) in H1 2025; AISC rose to $2,039/oz from $1,666/oz a year earlier on lower sales volumes and higher sustaining capex

Multiple analyst price-target increases following strong results and the gold rally: JPMorgan raised target to $140 (Overweight), RBC raised to $119 (Outperform); BMO downgraded to Market Perform ($115 target) and Citigroup trimmed target to $125, reflecting the stock's strong run; consensus remains Moderate Buy with an average target near $113

Ghana's new sliding-scale gold royalty regime (5-12%, reaching the 12% ceiling near current gold prices) and December 2026 deadline for transitioning mining services to Ghanaian-owned contractors came into sharper focus as a regulatory risk for AU's Obuasi and Iduapriem operations

items.notes: Reaffirmed despite the Obuasi KMS shaft closure following the April 2026 fatality; management expects to land near the midpoint (~3.0 Moz) aided by strong performance at the other nine operations
Based on an assumed gold price of approximately $4,250/oz; Q2 2026 AISC of $2,039/oz ran above the top of this range due to lower sales volumes and higher sustaining capex

Multi-year ramp-up via >$1 billion modernization/expansion/recapitalization program; higher-grade Block 11 access targeted around 2029; 2027 production expected broadly similar to 2026 as ramp continues
Approved by shareholders to align capital return framework with North American gold-mining peers, alongside the existing base dividend

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Alberto Calderon highlighted record cash generation and portfolio resilience in 2025-2026 ('This result shows the strong cash generation capacity of our assets, and the resilience of our portfolio'), while acknowledging the human cost of the April 2026 Obuasi fatality ('We are heartbroken by the loss of our colleague'). Management reiterated confidence in hitting FY2026 production guidance near the midpoint despite the KMS shaft closure, and emphasized a capital allocation framework prioritizing safe, well-capitalized operations, prudent debt levels (reinforced by the $666m bond buyback), and competitive shareholder returns via the new buyback program and growing dividend.

bull_case: Full, unhedged leverage to a record and still-rising gold price environment, with major banks forecasting $4,900-5,400+/oz through 2027 on sustained central bank buying and rate-cut tailwinds
Sukari (Egypt) has emerged as a genuine Tier 1 asset post-Centamin acquisition, delivering record production and ~$1.3bn EBITDA in FY2025, de-risking the growth thesis beyond legacy assets

Obuasi's multi-year ramp toward 400,000 oz/year by 2028 (with higher-grade ore from Block 11 around 2029) provides a multi-year, company-specific production growth path independent of exploration success elsewhere

Record free cash flow ($2.9bn FY2025) is funding both balance-sheet deleveraging (bond buybacks) and a new $2 billion share buyback program plus a growing dividend, aligning shareholder returns with North American peers
Geographic diversification across ten mines on four continents reduces single-asset catastrophic risk relative to peers with more concentrated portfolios
bear_case: Highest-cost producer among the gold majors (Q2 2026 AISC of $2,039/oz vs. Newmont ~$1,621/oz and Barrick ~$1,866/oz), meaning margins compress fastest among peers in any gold price pullback

Heavy concentration in politically higher-risk African jurisdictions (Ghana, DRC, Tanzania, Guinea) facing an active wave of resource nationalism - Ghana's new 5-12% sliding-scale royalty and December 2026 local-ownership mandate for mining services directly hit AU's Obuasi and Iduapriem operations

Recurring operational and safety incidents (April 2026 Obuasi fatality and shaft closure; January 2025 army/illegal-miner clash) highlight execution and security risk in underground, remote African operations
No corporate-level gold price hedge leaves the stock fully exposed if the current gold rally reverses on resolution of geopolitical tensions, a hawkish rate surprise, or slower central bank buying

Much of the current bull thesis (record gold prices, successful Sukari integration, buyback announcement) may already be reflected in the stock after a strong run, with several analysts (BMO downgrade, Citigroup target cut) turning more cautious near current levels
